  THE SUBMISSION RECEIPT LINKS, AND INHERITS NO STANDING.  It names the
  Slice /2 receipt — domain and name, as CD/0 data — and that is all it
  takes from it.  It is not a claim, not a basis, not a warrant, and it
  confers nothing on the petition it came from.  The standing that exists
  here belongs to the Slice /2 grant and stays there; the receipt is the
  LATER ACCOUNT of an earlier ACT, and an account of a thing is not the
  thing.  Note too what the name is: an IMAGE-LOCAL ORDINAL.  It is not
  durable, this file does not treat it as durable, and the field that
  carries it says so in its own name.

── one context occurrence TAG, two different sets of live bindings
  This section used to state ONE limitation.  Under policy v3 it states TWO
  DIFFERENT THINGS, and the difference is the whole of Review 1.
  
  SEAL-RESOLUTION-CONTEXT takes a host TAG.  Under policy v2 the tag WAS the
  context's whole identity, so two contexts declaring genuinely different
  things shared one submission occurrence identity and the layer recorded
  nothing that could tell them apart.  That was not an edge case and not a
  host's fault: the layer never asked what the references were declared to
  denote, so it could not record it.  IT WAS A DEFECT OF THIS LAYER.
  
  Under v3 the tag is a tag.  The context's IDENTITY is content-derived from
  its declarations.  Below, both halves are shown separately, because the
  residual never licensed the defect and the repair does not erase the
  residual.
  
  A.  SAME TAG, DIFFERENT DECLARATIONS.  Two contexts over two different
      witnesses.  Each support is declared with the witness's OWN governed
      Slice /0 identity, so the declarations differ because the declared
      objects differ.
